top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a defined and mature chemical invention, reversible fluorescent terminators on surface-bound templates, that turned a reaction cycle into a massively parallel digital readout, reproduced on independent platforms for two decades with consequences across biology and medicine. The Balasubramanian and Klenerman allocation rests on the documented integrated chemistry and working platform, and a citation worded around the chemistry keeps the scope honest. P002 is a sound, general catalyst-design achievement but follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize and has narrower reach, so I rank it second and above no award.
